text:
Nick Cousins came back from a concussion on Saturday, his first game since a huge hit from Jakob Chychrun ("I've never been hit that hard before," he said, in RMNB's headline). At 19:06 of the second period, with Ottawa trailing 1-0, Cousins tied it. Then Tim Stützle made the third period his.

For 39 minutes this was a Kings game on the scoreboard. Mats Zuccarello, recently back in the lineup, scored early off a Drew Doughty feed, and Anton Forsberg stopped Ridly Greig on a 33% chance in the first period, the best look Ottawa had all night. Los Angeles also had four power plays and created real danger on them (1.11 expected goals, the quality of chances) without scoring once.

Ottawa's edge was at even strength, where it out-chanced the Kings 1.98 to 0.89, and it finally showed. Cousins finished a feed from Jordan Spence and Jake Sanderson late in the second. Thirty seconds into the third, Stützle scored on a shot our numbers gave under a 1% chance, the kind of goal that changes a goalie's night. Stephen Halliday added a power-play goal at 5:54, and Stützle scored again at 7:16, both of his goals set up by Dylan Cozens. Quinton Byfield got one back for the Kings at 10:14, and Linus Ullmark handled the rest, finishing slightly better than the 21 shots he faced deserved.

Forsberg ended up 1.05 goals worse than expected on 28 shots,. Over the whole game Ottawa had 2.95 expected goals to 2.22 and wins this one 63% of the time in our replays of every shot, so the result was earned. Greig took the second star without a point, which tells you how much of the game ran through him.

It also settles the score from October, when the Kings won 6-5 in overtime. Off the ice, the Senators' week is about what comes next: Elliotte Friedman reported Ottawa's interest in Pittsburgh's Bryan Rust and Rickard Rakell, as Graeme Nichols of Coming Down the Pipe relayed.
headline: Cousins returns, Stützle takes over the third
